title: Removing the Square-Root Loss in XORP Bounds
summary: The χ² method proves full n-bit indifferentiable security for XORP and XORP[k], but a square-root loss spoils realistic bounds; whether refined analysis removes it remains open.

formal_statement.body: The $\chi^2$ analysis establishes full $n$-bit indifferentiable security for the $\mathrm{XORP}$ and $\mathrm{XORP}[k]$ constructions, but the square root in its bound prevents the result from yielding full $n$-bit security for realistic parameter choices. Determine whether a more sophisticated application of the $\chi^2$ method can eliminate this square-root loss from the indifferentiability bounds for both constructions.

scope.domain: Symmetric-cryptographic indifferentiability analysis of XORP and XORP[k] using the χ² method.
parameters: n: bit length defining the full-security target
k: parameter indexing the XORP[k] construction
scope.unresolved_remainder: Whether a more sophisticated χ² analysis can eliminate the square-root loss from the indifferentiability bounds for both XORP and XORP[k].

citations.label: Full Indifferentiable Security of the Xor of Two or More Random Permutations Using the \chi ^2 Method

progress.summary: The paper establishes full n-bit indifferentiable security for XORP and XORP[k], while noting that the square root in its bounds prevents practical full security. It presents removing this loss through a more sophisticated χ² application as an immediate goal.
citation_labels: Srimanta Bhattacharya et al., Full Indifferentiable Security of the Xor of Two or More Random Permutations Using the \chi ^2 Method
